meanings.164.302: Establish which regulated activities and electronic protected health information are within the organization's Security Rule scope.
meanings.164.306(a): Protect ePHI confidentiality, integrity and availability against the threats relevant to the organization and its workforce.
meanings.164.306(b): Select safeguards appropriate to the organization's environment and risks, documenting why the chosen approach is reasonable for that scope.
meanings.164.306(c): Account for the applicable Security Rule standards across the ePHI scope rather than treating selected technical controls as the whole program.
meanings.164.306(d): Distinguish required specifications from addressable decisions. Addressable still requires an evaluation and a documented, appropriate decision; it does not mean optional.
meanings.164.306(e): Keep safeguards relevant as the environment and risks change; implementation is not a one-time documentation exercise.
meanings.164.308(a)(1)(i): Use a coordinated process to identify ePHI risks, select responses and review whether security practices operate as intended.
meanings.164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A): Understand the risks to ePHI across its actual locations, uses and dependencies, including weaknesses and potential consequences.
meanings.164.308(a)(1)(ii)(B): Turn the risk analysis into selected safeguards and tracked decisions about reducing the identified exposure.
meanings.164.308(a)(1)(ii)(C): Establish and apply an appropriate response when workforce members do not follow security policies and procedures.
meanings.164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D): Review records of system activity to identify inappropriate access or other security concerns and document follow-up.
meanings.164.308(a)(2): Identify the person responsible for developing and implementing Security Rule policies and procedures.
meanings.164.308(a)(3)(i): Manage workforce access so people can perform authorized duties without retaining inappropriate access to ePHI.
meanings.164.308(a)(3)(ii)(A): Decide how workforce access and work involving ePHI are authorized or supervised.
meanings.164.308(a)(3)(ii)(B): Establish how the organization determines whether a workforce member's access to ePHI is appropriate.
meanings.164.308(a)(3)(ii)(C): Remove access when a person leaves or the basis for their access changes.
meanings.164.308(a)(4)(i): Manage authorization and permissions for ePHI through deliberate access procedures.
meanings.164.308(a)(4)(ii)(A): Where clearinghouse functions sit within a larger organization, address separation from access by other organizational components.
meanings.164.308(a)(4)(ii)(B): Define how access to ePHI is approved, including the relevant systems, workstations and activities.
meanings.164.308(a)(4)(ii)(C): Establish, review and change access in accordance with the organization's authorization decisions.
meanings.164.308(a)(5)(i): Give the workforce a security awareness and training program that supports safe handling of ePHI.
meanings.164.308(a)(5)(ii)(A): Use security reminders to reinforce workforce awareness beyond initial training.
meanings.164.308(a)(5)(ii)(B): Address malicious software through appropriate prevention, detection and reporting practices.
meanings.164.308(a)(5)(ii)(C): Monitor login activity and address discrepancies that may indicate inappropriate access.
meanings.164.308(a)(5)(ii)(D): Establish practices for creating, changing and protecting passwords used to access ePHI.
meanings.164.308(a)(6)(i): Maintain a usable process for handling suspected and known security incidents.
meanings.164.308(a)(6)(ii): Identify and respond to incidents, address harmful effects where practicable and retain the incident and outcome record.
meanings.164.308(a)(7)(i): Plan how ePHI and critical operations will be protected and recovered during disruptive events.
meanings.164.308(a)(7)(ii)(A): Maintain recoverable copies of ePHI as part of the organization's contingency approach.
meanings.164.308(a)(7)(ii)(B): Define how lost data will be restored following a disruptive event.
meanings.164.308(a)(7)(ii)(C): Protect ePHI while critical business processes operate under emergency conditions.
meanings.164.308(a)(7)(ii)(D): Test and revise contingency procedures so the plan remains usable in the actual environment.
meanings.164.308(a)(7)(ii)(E): Understand which applications and data are most critical to support contingency priorities.
meanings.164.308(a)(8): Evaluate whether technical and nontechnical safeguards continue to meet the program's applicable security requirements.
meanings.164.308(b)(1): Address the safeguards and assurances associated with business associates handling ePHI on the organization's behalf.
meanings.164.308(b)(3): Retain the written contract or other permitted arrangement supporting the relevant business-associate assurances.
meanings.164.310(a)(1): Limit physical access to facilities and systems while allowing properly authorized access.
meanings.164.310(a)(2)(i): Plan for appropriate facility access needed to support restoration and emergency operations.
meanings.164.310(a)(2)(ii): Protect facilities and equipment against unauthorized physical access, tampering and theft.
meanings.164.310(a)(2)(iii): Validate physical access according to roles and needs, including visitors and maintenance personnel.
meanings.164.310(a)(2)(iv): Retain records of physical-security-related repairs and modifications to facility components.
meanings.164.310(b): Define appropriate workstation use and the physical surroundings for work involving ePHI.
meanings.164.310(c): Apply physical safeguards that restrict access to workstations used for ePHI.
meanings.164.310(d)(1): Control devices and media containing ePHI as they move into, out of and within the organization.
meanings.164.310(d)(2)(i): Dispose of ePHI and the media holding it through appropriate documented procedures.
meanings.164.310(d)(2)(ii): Remove ePHI appropriately before media are made available for reuse.
meanings.164.310(d)(2)(iii): Track relevant hardware and media movements and the people responsible for them.
meanings.164.310(d)(2)(iv): Consider backup and storage needs before equipment containing ePHI is moved.
meanings.164.312(a)(1): Use technical access controls so ePHI is available to authorized people or software processes.
meanings.164.312(a)(2)(i): Identify users uniquely so system access and activity can be attributed appropriately.
meanings.164.312(a)(2)(ii): Provide a controlled way to obtain necessary ePHI during an emergency.
meanings.164.312(a)(2)(iii): Address unattended sessions through an appropriate automatic-logoff decision and implementation.
meanings.164.312(a)(2)(iv): Evaluate and implement an appropriate approach to encrypting and decrypting ePHI within the assessed scope.
meanings.164.312(b): Record and examine activity in systems containing or using ePHI.
meanings.164.312(c)(1): Protect ePHI against improper alteration or destruction.
meanings.164.312(c)(2): Use an appropriate mechanism to confirm that ePHI has not been altered or destroyed improperly.
meanings.164.312(d): Verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one it claims to be.
meanings.164.312(e)(1): Protect ePHI against unauthorized access while it is transmitted over an electronic communications network.
meanings.164.312(e)(2)(i): Address the integrity of transmitted ePHI so inappropriate changes can be detected or prevented as applicable.
meanings.164.312(e)(2)(ii): Evaluate transmission encryption in the actual environment and document the addressability decision and supporting implementation.
meanings.164.314(a)(1): Connect applicable business-associate arrangements to the security responsibilities established in those arrangements.
meanings.164.314(b)(1): Where applicable, address the group health plan and plan-sponsor arrangements that support protection of ePHI.
meanings.164.316(a): Maintain policies and procedures that describe how the organization implements its security requirements.
meanings.164.316(b)(1): Retain the documentation needed to demonstrate required policies, procedures, actions and decisions.
meanings.164.316(b)(2)(i): Apply the documentation-retention rule to the relevant records, including the appropriate starting point for retention.
meanings.164.316(b)(2)(ii): Make required documentation available to those responsible for implementing the procedures it describes.
meanings.164.316(b)(2)(iii): Review and update documentation in response to relevant environmental or operational changes.
meanings.164.105: Document the entity structure and designated components relevant to the organization's HIPAA responsibilities.
meanings.164.402: Document the analysis supporting a breach determination or an applicable exception; do not equate every security event with the same notification outcome.
meanings.164.404: Where individual notification applies, track the affected population, content, timing and delivery through the responsible process.
meanings.164.406: Evaluate and manage media notification when the applicable breach conditions require it.
meanings.164.408: Manage the applicable reporting to the Secretary and maintain the supporting smaller-breach records where relevant.
meanings.164.410: Coordinate business-associate notice to the covered entity when an applicable breach is identified.
meanings.164.412: Document and manage a law-enforcement-related delay in notification when the applicable conditions are met.
meanings.164.414: Retain the administrative records and evidence supporting notification compliance or the decision that notice was not required.
meanings.164.530: Connect relevant Privacy administration responsibilities to the security program without treating this supporting unit as a full Privacy Rule assessment.

164.302.implementation: Typical implementation maps regulated activities, ePHI locations and accountable functions into a usable scope statement. Include hosted services and relevant business-associate relationships.
164.302.evidence: Entity/scope statement; ePHI data-flow map; systems inventory; relevant service-provider register.

164.306.implementation: Typical implementation connects the chosen safeguards to documented scope, risk decisions and maintenance triggers. Record the reason for environment-specific choices rather than relying on a generic checklist.
164.306.evidence: Security program description; risk analysis; safeguard decisions; policy review and change records.

164.308.implementation: Typical implementation gives this administrative process an owner, a documented operating approach and records showing that it is used. Check coverage across the relevant workforce, systems and service providers; distinguish a written plan from evidence of execution.
164.308.evidence: The procedure and dated records for this activity, such as risk decisions, access approvals, workforce training, incident records, contingency tests or business-associate arrangements, as relevant to this specification.

164.310.implementation: Typical implementation connects physical safeguards and media handling to the relevant facilities, workstations and device lifecycle. Document who is responsible and how visitors, moves, disposal and exceptions are handled where applicable.
164.310.evidence: Facility/access procedures; access or visitor records; workstation protections; maintenance, media movement or disposal records relevant to this item.

164.312.implementation: Typical implementation identifies the ePHI systems covered by the technical safeguard, demonstrates its actual configuration and documents exclusions or alternative measures. A product's capability alone does not show that the protection is enabled across scope.
164.312.evidence: Scoped system configuration exports; account/access records; audit-event samples; integrity checks or transmission protection settings relevant to this specification.

164.314.implementation: Typical implementation connects the relevant organizational arrangement to responsible parties, written terms and evidence that the arrangement is maintained.
164.314.evidence: Applicable agreements or plan documents; assigned responsibilities; review and amendment records.

164.316.implementation: Typical implementation maintains controlled, accessible documentation with owners, version history and retention handling. Check how changes are incorporated and how older required records remain available.
164.316.evidence: Policy/procedure register; approval/version history; retention settings; documentation access and update records.

support.implementation: Depending on applicability, identify the responsible process, record the decision and link the supporting records. Escalate legal notification or entity-structure decisions to the appropriate qualified owner; this supporting assessment does not replace that decision.
support.evidence: Applicable entity/role documentation, incident and breach analysis, notification decisions, correspondence or relevant administrative procedures. Avoid unnecessary patient information in assessment notes.
